Wirtinger inequality, named after [Wilhelm Wirtinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_Wirtinger), is a fundamental result in [complex linear algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_algebra) which relates the symplectic and volume forms of a [hermitian inner product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermitian_inner_product).

Witt vector cohomology was an early [p-adic cohomology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P-adic_cohomology) theory for [algebraic varieties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algebraic_varieties) introduced by .

Witten conjecture is a conjecture about [intersection number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intersection_number)s of stable classes on the [moduli space of curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moduli_space_of_curves), introduced by [Edward Witten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Witten) in the paper , and generalized in .
Wittgenstein's rod is a problem in [geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometry) discussed by 20th-century philosopher [Ludwig Wittgenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Wittgenstein).

Wolfgang von Wersin (3 December 188213 June 1976) was a [Czech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czechs)-born designer, painter, architect and author who developed his career in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany).

[Wenjun Wu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu_Wenjun)'s method is an algorithm for solving [multivariate polynomial equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_of_polynomial_equations) introduced in the late 1970s by the Chinese [mathematician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematician) [Wen-Tsun Wu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu_Wenjun).

Wu–Yang dictionary refers to the mathematical identification that allows back-and-forth translation between the concepts of [gauge theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauge_theory) and those of [differential geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_geometry).

y-homeomorphism, or crosscap slide, is a special type of auto-[homeomorphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeomorphism) in [non-orientable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orientability) [surface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_(topology))s.

Yamabe invariant, also referred to as the sigma constant, is a real number invariant associated to a [smooth manifold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_manifold) that is preserved under [diffeomorphisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffeomorphisms).
Yamabe problem refers to a conjecture in the mathematical field of [differential geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_geometry), which was resolved in the 1980s.

Yang–Baxter operators are [invertible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertible) linear [endomorphisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endomorphisms) with applications in [theoretical physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physics) and [topology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topology).

Yang–Mills flow is a [gradient flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_flow) described by the [Yang–Mills equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang–Mills_equations), hence a method to describe a [gradient descent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent) of the Yang–Mills action functional.

Yang–Mills moduli space (short YM moduli space, also instanton moduli space) is the [moduli space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moduli_space) of the [Yang–Mills equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang–Mills_equations), hence the space of its solutions up to gauge.

Yang–Mills–Higgs flow is a [gradient flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_flow) described by the [Yang–Mills–Higgs equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang–Mills–Higgs_equations), hence a method to describe a [gradient descent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent) of the Yang–Mills–Higgs action functional.

Yao graph, named after [Andrew Yao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Yao), is a kind of [geometric spanner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometric_spanner), a weighted [undirected graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undirected_graph) connecting a set of [geometric points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_(geometry)) with the property that, for every pair of points in the graph, their [shortest path](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shortest_path) has a length that is within a constant factor of their [Euclidean distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_distance).

Yau's conjecture is a [mathematical conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_conjecture) which states that any closed [Riemannian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemannian_manifold) [3-manifold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3-manifold) has infinitely many [[Differentiable_manifold#Definition|smooth]] [closed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed_manifold) [[Immersion (mathematics)#Immersed plane curves|immersed]] [minimal surface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_surface)s.

term: Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue
page: Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue
definition: Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue is, as of 2018, an unsolved [conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjecture) proposed by [Shing-Tung Yau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shing-Tung_Yau) in 1982.

Yusu Wang is a Chinese computer scientist and mathematician who works as a professor at the [Halıcıoğlu Data Science Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halıcıoğlu_Data_Science_Institute) at the [University of California, San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_San_Diego) .

Zariski space, named for [Oscar Zariski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Zariski), has several different meanings: *A topological space that is [Noetherian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noetherian_space) (every open set is quasicompact) *A topological space that is Noetherian and also [sober](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sober_space) (every nonempty closed irreducible subset is the closure of a unique point).

Zariski tangent space is a construction that defines a [tangent space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangent_space) at a point P on an [algebraic variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algebraic_variety) V (and more generally).
Zariski's connectedness theorem (due to [Oscar Zariski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Zariski)) says that under certain conditions the fibers of a morphism of varieties are connected.

Zariski's main theorem, proved by , is a statement about the structure of [birational morphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birational_morphism)s stating roughly that there is only one branch at any normal point of a [variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algebraic_variety).

Zariski–Riemann space or Zariski space of a [subring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_(mathematics)) k of a [field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_(mathematics)) K is a [locally ringed space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locally_ringed_space) whose points are [valuation ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valuation_ring)s containing k and contained in K.
Zener ratio is a dimensionless number that is used to quantify the [anisotropy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anisotropy) for [cubic crystals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubic_crystal_system).

zigzag is a [pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattern) like a row of Ws joined together, consisting of a single line made up of line segments of usually constant length joined by usually constant angles in alternating directions.

Zilber–Pink conjecture is a far-reaching generalisation of many famous [Diophantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diophantine_geometry) conjectures and statements, such as [André–Oort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/André–Oort_conjecture), [[Arithmetic of abelian varieties#Manin–Mumford conjecture|Manin–Mumford]], and [Mordell–Lang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mordell–Lang_conjecture).

Zimmert set is a set of positive integers associated with the structure of quotients of [hyperbolic three-space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperbolic_3-space) by a [Bianchi group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bianchi_group).

Zoll surface, named after [Otto Zoll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto_Zoll), is a [surface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_(topology)) [homeomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeomorphic) to the [2-sphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2-sphere), equipped with a [Riemannian metric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemannian_metric) all of whose [geodesic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geodesic)s are [closed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed_geodesic) and of equal length.

Zonal and meridional flow are [direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relative_direction)s and [region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Region)s of [fluid flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid_flow) on a [globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globe).
zone theorem is a result that establishes the complexity of the zone of a line in an [arrangement of lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrangement_of_lines).
zonoid is a type of [centrally symmetric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_symmetry) [convex body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_body).

zonotope is a [convex polytope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_polytope) that can be described as the [Minkowski sum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minkowski_addition) of a finite set of line segments in of the ambient space, the zonotope is a parallelotope.

étale or algebraic fundamental group is an analogue in [algebraic geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algebraic_geometry), for [schemes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scheme_(mathematics)), of the usual [fundamental group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_group) of [topological space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topological_space)s.

étale homotopy type is an analogue of the [homotopy type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homotopy_type) of [topological space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topological_space)s for [algebraic varieties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algebraic_variety).

étale topology is a [Grothendieck topology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck_topology) on the category of [scheme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scheme_(mathematics))s which has properties similar to the Euclidean topology, but unlike the Euclidean topology, it is also defined in positive [characteristic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Characteristic_(algebra)).
ε-net (pronounced [epsilon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epsilon)-net) is the approximation of a general set by a collection of simpler subsets.

∞-Chern–Simons theory (not to be confused with [infinite-dimensional Chern–Simons theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinite-dimensional_Chern–Simons_theory)) is a generalized formulation of [Chern–Simons theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chern–Simons_theory) from [differential geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_geometry) using the formalism of [higher category theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_category_theory), which in particular studies [∞-categories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/∞-categories).

∞-Chern–Weil theory is a generalized formulation of [Chern–Weil theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chern–Weil_theory) from [differential geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_geometry) using the formalism of [higher category theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_category_theory).
